title: Lot Saved, and Shu'ayb Calls His People

paragraphs.text: Lot spoke to his people as their brother. He asked them why they did not fear Allah, and he told them that he was a trustworthy messenger sent to them. He called them to fear Allah and obey him. Like the messengers before him, he did not ask for any payment, because his reward comes only from the Lord of the worlds. Then he spoke against their sin. They went to men with desire and left the wives whom their Lord had created for them. He told them plainly that they were a people who had crossed the limits.

Instead of listening, the people threatened him. They said that if he did not stop, he would surely be thrown out of the town. Lot replied that he truly hated what they were doing. Then he turned to his Lord in prayer and asked Him to save him and his family from the result of their deeds. So Allah saved him and all his family, except an old woman who stayed behind with the others. Then Allah destroyed the rest of them. He sent down upon them a rain of stones, and terrible was the rain that fell on those who had been warned. In this story there is a sign, although most of them did not believe. Indeed, the Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.

Next, the story moves to another nation. The companions of the thicket, which was a place of thick trees, also denied the messengers. Their messenger Shu'ayb came to them and asked them the same important question: "Will you not fear Allah?" He began his call in the same way as the messengers who came before him.

hardWords.m: a place with many trees and bushes close together
